policies.summary: When certifying a major utility facility (over 75 MW), the Public Service Commission may refuse to apply a local law or regulation it finds unreasonably restrictive as applied to the facility, and must state its reasons in its order.

Any electric generating plant able to run at more than 75 MW is a major utility facility that needs a certificate of environmental compatibility and public convenience and necessity from the Public Service Commission before construction; smaller plants are left to county and municipal land use control.

policies.state_body: South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (enforcement)
policies.summary: In a county with neither rural zoning nor a solar ordinance, a solar energy system with a footprint over 13 acres must meet state default standards: 50 ft setback from property lines and road rights of way, 200 ft from the nearest residence, church or school, 15 ft maximum height, a vegetative buffer, fencing and a decommissioning plan, after a county public hearing; the Department of Environmental Services enforces with civil penalties.

restrictions.description: County's Unified Development Code does not specifically define data centers or battery energy storage systems; council sought to close a loophole after learning of a proposed "Project 59" data center in the county industrial park, and to give time to set standards for setbacks, buffers, noise, lighting, and emergency access. Active as of 2026-09-23; adopted unanimously on third and final reading Sept. 14, 2026, following a public hearing. Pauses land-use and development approvals for data centers and battery storage facilities outside areas zoned Industrial I or Industrial II; does not affect the proposed Project 59 data center, which is sited in an Industrial I district and received a conditional-use determination from county planning staff. Legal basis: Ordinance 2026-18 (Clarendon County Council).

County has no zoning provisions for battery energy storage systems or data centers; follows public opposition to, and council's rejection of, a proposed 1,700-acre solar farm. Active as of 2026-09-23. The 60-day emergency moratorium (26-1049, effective June 23, 2026) lapsed around Aug. 22, 2026, but Council gave unanimous third and final reading to the three companion 180-day ordinances (26-1050 Solar, 26-1051 BESS, 26-1052 Data Centers) at its Aug. 11, 2026 regular meeting, per the county's own posted minutes, so the pause on new permits for solar, BESS, and data-center facilities has run continuously and is now due to run to roughly 2027-02-07. Separately, the county's Land Use Committee and Planning Commission continued work in August-September 2026 on permanent, non-moratorium data-center zoning standards (OA-26-01), which received first reading Sept. 8, 2026 and had not been adopted as of this date. Legal basis: Emergency Ordinance 26-1049 (60-day moratorium on BESS, data centers, and solar farms, approved and effective June 23, 2026, since lapsed); superseded by Ordinances 26-1050 (Solar), 26-1051 (BESS), and 26-1052 (Data Centers), each imposing a 180-day moratorium, given second reading July 21, 2026 and unanimous third/final reading August 11, 2026 per the county's posted regular-meeting minutes.
